title: Optics Meets the Switch: Celestica Introduces the DS6005 for 1.6T AI Fabrics
summary: Discover how Celestica's DS6005 1.6T switching platform uses co-packaged optics (CPO) to scale AI data center fabrics, reduce power, and increase bandwidth density.

Amit Thakkar,


Vice President, Product Management

AI data center infrastructure is reaching a system-level inflection point. Accelerated computing is driving larger clusters for frontier AI training and inference, placing new demands on the data center networks connecting thousands of GPUs. As these fabrics move to 1.6T and beyond, they must deliver more bandwidth without exhausting available power, cooling, rack space, or signal-integrity budgets.


Higher per-lane rates, from 56G and 112G to 224G and eventually 448G, make the signal integrity across the electrical path between switch silicon and front-panel optics increasingly challenging. Hyperscalers and other AI Infrastructure Builders need a fabric architecture that can scale performance and capacity within the physical and operational limits of the data center.


Co-packaged optics (CPO) addresses this challenge by placing optical engines adjacent to the switch ASIC on the same package substrate. Shortening the high-speed electrical path from centimeters to millimeters can reduce channel impairments and reliance on power-intensive signal conditioning while increasing bandwidth density.


CPO is not a universal replacement for pluggable optics. It is an architectural choice for environments where power per bit, reach, density, and tightly coupled accelerator traffic outweigh the flexibility of discrete optics.


Figure 1: Co-packaged optics potential benefits


## Lower Power


Shorter electrical paths and reduced reliance on DSPs (Digital Signal Processor) and retimers can lower link-level power compared with traditional retimed pluggable implementations. This can help ease rack-level power and cooling constraints as AI fabrics scale.


## Lower Latency


Shorter electrical paths and fewer signal-conditioning stages can reduce latency while improving signal integrity. The benefit depends on the topology, optics, and protocol implementation. A near-term opportunity is in latency-sensitive scale-up networks, where accelerator-to-accelerator communication is particularly sensitive to delay.


## Higher Bandwidth Density


Moving optical engines into the switch package frees front-panel space traditionally occupied by data-bearing QSFP and OSFP modules. Compact interfaces such as MMC (Miniature Multi-Fiber Connector) can increase faceplate bandwidth density while changing how operators allocate rack space, cooling, and cabling across dense AI deployments.


## Introducing Celestica DS6005


Celestica is introducing DS6005, a 1.6T co-packaged optics data center switching platform built for dense AI scale-up and scale-out fabrics.


[DS6005](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6005/) utilizes the latest Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson switch chip, which moves the optical engines onto the same package substrate as the switch ASIC and removes pluggable optics from the front panel. The platform brings switching, optical engines, liquid cooling, software, and lasers together as one integrated system.


Figure 2: Celestica DS6005 utilizing the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson switch chip


Figure 2.1: Celestica DS6005 utilizing the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson switch chip


This architecture helps AI infrastructure builders increase bandwidth density and reduce fabric power while retaining open networking, topology flexibility, and a serviceable external laser architecture. DS6005 consumes lower power than pluggable systems when measured against the approved baseline, optical configuration, measurement boundary, and test method.


DS6005 is a compact, fully liquid-cooled ORv3 system designed for high-density AI infrastructure. Per-switch power savings can compound across a fabric as the number of switches grows across scale-up and scale-out deployments. The resulting fabric-level savings will depend on the size, topology, and operating model of each deployment.


Laser source serviceability is also built into the DS6005 architecture. It includes external laser source interfaces and field-replaceable ELS (External Laser Source) modules. Operators can service an external laser module on the system independently.


The platform supports breakout modes from 1.6T to 800G, 400G, and 200G, allowing AI Infrastructure Builders to adapt the system to different accelerator generations and cluster topologies.


DS6005 is designed for open operations with[SONiC Plus by Celestica](https://cls.celestica.com/software/celestica-sonic/) . The enterprise-ready network operating system includes software capabilities for managing optical engines, external laser modules, and photonic diagnostics. This gives infrastructure teams an open, supported operating foundation without placing the full burden of software integration and lifecycle support on their own engineers.


## Where CPO Fits in the AI Fabric


CPO can support both scale-up and scale-out AI back-end fabrics, but its strongest differentiation is in high-bandwidth scale-up environments. As electrical interconnects become more constrained by reach, signal integrity, and power at higher lane rates, CPO provides an optical path for tightly coupled accelerator communication.


In multi-rack pods, reach and power per bit become increasingly important. Density, topology, cabling, cooling, serviceability, and lifecycle operations should be evaluated together rather than as separate component decisions.


CPO can also provide power-efficient fiber connectivity for scale-out fabrics. The use case and economics should be assessed against the flexibility of pluggable optics for each deployment.


## One Platform, Different AI Infrastructure Priorities


DS6005 gives different types of AI Infrastructure Builders a common CPO platform that can be evaluated against their specific requirements for scale, bandwidth, power, latency, flexibility, and lifecycle operations.


Hyperscalers need predictable power, cooling, fabric density, and operational consistency across large AI clusters. DS6005 combines 1.6T connectivity, a liquid-cooled ORv3 form factor, high bandwidth density, and an open control model for environments where fleet-level efficiency matters.


NeoCloud providers need to bring capacity online quickly, maximize accelerator capacity per rack, and preserve the flexibility to support changing workloads and GPU generations. A dense CPO tier can help manage power and floor-space constraints while maintaining a software-defined operating model through SONiC Plus by Celestica.


AI Labs need high-bandwidth fabrics that support rapid experimentation without locking research infrastructure into a closed stack. DS6005 can be evaluated where low-latency accelerator communication, density, and open networking are priorities, with serviceability and supply chain requirements considered early in the architecture process.


## From Open Architecture to AI Advantage


CPO changes the optics decision from a front-panel component selection into a system design decision spanning switching, optics, cooling, software, cabling, and serviceability.


The question is not whether CPO should replace every pluggable optic. Co-packaged optics can provide the required scale, power efficiency, density, reach, and lifecycle operating model for modern AI data centers.


Celestica DS6005 gives AI Infrastructure Builders a concrete 1.6T CPO platform for evaluating those tradeoffs within open ORv3 environments. Combined with SONiC Plus by Celestica, joint engineering, global manufacturing capacity, and enterprise-class services, DS6005 helps transform open architecture principles from the OCP Community into AI advantage.


CPO and pluggable systems will coexist as infrastructure builders optimize each fabric tier for performance, economics, flexibility, and operational risk.
